An effect answers for its joins seam by seam (rich-animation-27tq.19d)

Review of #529. Summing joins across both sides let a join broken on one side
hide a new one on the other. The docs now say the ring is the outer edge.

A box frame is its own fact on a Style, and an effect answers for its own joins (rich-animation-27tq.19d)

Review of #529. A frame stamped row 0, col 0 on every cell was a false Anchor
and reached WidgetMouseEvent.cell; it is now Style.boxFrame, which draws
nothing and claims no position. standsApart blamed every effect for a join the
child drew, so typewriter and backspace threw as marchingAnts did. A box with no
ink holds still, and a table too narrow for its edges draws no frame.

A marching-ants border is a library effect (rich-animation-27tq.19d)

marchingAnts marches the frame of whatever box an element draws, at every
box set and width, past a title. A frame is told by what drew it, never by
its glyphs: Box.frame stamps one drawing's cells with an owner, as a strip's
seam is told, so a user's container reaches it the way Panel and Table do.

The ring is read off where a frame's cells sit in the element, because a
Table draws its top rule before it knows its height.

It stays out of GLYPH_EFFECT_CATALOGUE: that record is the names a template's
glyphs takes, and a template fragment has no box, so the name could never
march. The playground's glyph-matching march is removed.
